content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Lewis McFadden's PostLewis McFadden Verified account4d · Shared with PublicThey just flew around the Moon and made history... And the “extra pay” for that 10 day mission? About the price of a coffee each day.NASA’s Artemis II astronauts are salaried government employees, typically paid on the federal General Schedule, often around the GS 13 to GS 14 range, which puts their annual pay roughly in the six figures, commonly around $120,000 to $190,000 depending on experience and locality. Recent reporting places the current figure for the U.S. crew at around $152,000 a year.But for flying farther from Earth than any humans since Apollo, the only additional compensation is a tiny incidental stipend of about $5 a day, which means roughly $50 total for the entire 10-day lunar mission.They were literally circling the Moon, risking their lives on one of humanity’s most historic missions, and the “extra” pay is less than what many people spend on lunch.Of course, astronauts do not do this for the money.They do it for science, exploration, and the chance to be part of something bigger than themselves.Still, it is one of those facts that instantly puts things into perspective. Some jobs pay millions for entertainment. Some pay bonuses for quarterly targets. And then there are people who leave Earth for $5 a day extra.Sometimes the biggest story is not what they earn.
